scope: Two previously identified adult registry reports and narrowly scoped scale-definition checks; original extraction only.

cohort_overlap.classification: potentially overlapping reports; not independent cohorts
cohort_overlap.basis: Both reports use the Calgary adult registry begun in 2021; the later analysis also includes Paris.

reports.title: Toxin for Tics: Practical Guidance for Clinicians from a Registry-Based Naturalistic Study
reports.design: Treatment-description analysis within prospective single-site clinical registry; nonrandomized ever-versus-never botulinum-toxin comparison at registration.
reports.site: Movement Disorders Clinic, Calgary, Alberta, Canada

population.childhood_onset_distribution: Not separately reported; diagnoses use DSM-5 criteria.
population.selection_limits: Clinical specialty care; no population sampling or severe-only entry criterion.

missingness.imputation_or_model: No longitudinal outcome model or missingness analysis reported.
missingness.caution: Completion at interim analysis is not automatically permanent loss to follow-up.

registry_collection.measure: YGTSS tic inventory, tic severity and tic-related impairment
registry_collection.visits: Registration, six and twelve months named in registry methods

registry_collection.measure: Gilles de la Tourette Quality of Life scale
Presence and severity of psychiatric comorbidities

published_comparisons.exposure_definition: Ever botulinum toxin during enrollment versus never
published_comparisons.interpretation: Unadjusted selection-related group contrasts; not a severity-burden correlation or a causal treatment effect. Test tails are not specified in the methods; p values are retained verbatim, not re-derived.

treatment_context.injection_detail_missing_reason: One participant treated by another team

relationships_of_interest.meaning_of_null: Not reported, not evidence of zero association

reports.access: Corresponding-author request subject to privacy/ethical restrictions; no project access granted.
reports.funding_conflicts: No specific funding and no relevant conflicts declared; additional author financial disclosures listed in source.
reports.correction_check: No notice identified in limited inspected source/title checks; not comprehensive clearance.

reports.title: The Phenomenology of Tics in Adults: Data From the Calgary and Paris Adult Tic Disorders Registry
reports.design: Cross-sectional first clinical assessment from prospective registry
sites: Foothills Hospital Movement Disorder Clinic, Calgary

population.definition: Adults with childhood-onset DSM-5 primary chronic tic disorders during routine clinical care
exclusions: coexisting primary tics and functional tic-like behaviors
population.selection_limits: Expert-center referral population; severe status not an inclusion criterion.

assessment.time: First clinical assessment only in this analysis
assessment.instrument: Yale Global Tic Severity Scale, revised version
assessment.QoL_collection_for_this_analysis: No QoL outcome reported; future research discussed
assessment.Paris_six_twelve_visit_availability: Not established by this cross-sectional report

first_assessment_summaries.interval_note: Intervals are reproduced as printed; Table 2 itself lacks a precision label. No new precision estimate is calculated.

psychiatric_data.ascertainment: DSM-5 clinical examination or psychiatric diagnostic consultation

treatment_data.context: Medication classes at first assessment; not an untreated sample
treatment_data.inconsistency: Antipsychotic subgroups sum to 99, not 95; unresolved. Present in indexed PMC and publisher PDF text. Do not silently repair or pool.

reports.published_association_scope: Sex contrasts in phenomenology, severity, impairment, comorbidities and treatments; no severity-to-burden or QoL model.

listed: S1 motor tic phenomenology by sex
S2 phonic tic phenomenology by sex
supplements.reason: Not required to establish main-report endpoint scope; captions checked only.

reports.funding_conflicts: University of Calgary Owerko Centre and Association Francaise du Syndrome Gilles de La Tourette support; no conflicts declared.
reports.access: Restricted corresponding-author request; no project permission granted.
reports.correction_check: No notice identified in limited inspected source/title checks; not comprehensive clearance.

supporting_scale_sources.use: Primary development abstract: 27 patient-reported items; psychological, physical, obsessional and cognitive dimensions. Not registry data.
Primary indexed scale-method text: standard original GTS-QOL past-four-week recall, 0–4 items and normalized 0–100 subscales, higher worse. Actual registry version/language/scoring not established.
Primary mixed-age benchmark methods and classification caveats; not an adult registry endpoint validation.
supporting_scale_sources.global_score_definition: Total tic 0–50 plus impairment 0–50 gives global 0–100.
supporting_scale_sources.threshold_caution: Table 3 prints marked 28–43 and severe 43–46; fair agreement with CGI-S. No threshold adopted.

actual_conclusions.severity_as_burden_surrogate: Not validated or directly tested in the two reports; preserve separate outcomes.
actual_conclusions.substantive_predicted_association: Untested by this extraction's core reports, not confirmed by absent analysis.
actual_conclusions.fully_operational_severe_estimand: No: threshold, adult/diagnosis applicability and visit windows require definition.
actual_conclusions.candidate_estimand: Observed-visit persistence at 0/6/12 months during clinical care, conditional on an agreed diagnosis-appropriate threshold; parallel independent burden distributions.
